questions.question: Which of the following is a natural method of contraception?
questions.explanation: Natural methods avoid drugs or devices: periodic abstinence, withdrawal and lactational amenorrhoea (breastfeeding suppresses ovulation for up to six months).

questions.question: Copper-releasing IUDs act by
options: releasing Cu ions that suppress sperm motility and fertilising capacity
questions.explanation: Copper IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) are effective for years; hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20) add a hormonal effect.

questions.question: Saheli is a
options: non-steroidal oral contraceptive pill taken once a week
questions.explanation: Developed by CDRI Lucknow, Saheli's non-steroidal nature and weekly dosage make it a favourite NCERT fact.

questions.question: Emergency contraceptives are effective if taken within
questions.explanation: They work by preventing ovulation, fertilisation or implantation — they are NOT abortifacients, which is why the timing matters.

questions.question: Vasectomy is
options: the surgical cutting and tying of the vas deferens in males
questions.explanation: Tubectomy in females ties the fallopian tubes; both are sterilisation methods with a low failure rate but are essentially irreversible.

questions.question: Which of the following is a bacterial STI?
questions.explanation: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and chlamydiasis are bacterial; genital herpes and AIDS are viral; trichomoniasis is protozoan.

questions.question: Amniocentesis is misused for
options: sex determination of the foetus, which is illegal in India
questions.explanation: It has a legitimate use in detecting genetic abnormalities, but its misuse for sex determination led to a statutory ban on such use.

questions.question: Infertility in couples can be treated by
options: assisted reproductive technologies such as IVF and IUI
questions.explanation: ART includes IVF (test-tube babies), ZIFT, GIFT, ICSI and IUI — each suited to a different cause of infertility.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Reproductive Health

questions.question: In ZIFT, the zygote or early embryo (up to 8 blastomeres) is transferred into the
questions.explanation: ZIFT = zygote intra fallopian transfer; IUT (embryo transfer into the uterus) is used for embryos with more than 8 blastomeres.

questions.question: GIFT stands for
questions.explanation: In GIFT, gametes from a donor are transferred into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ova but can support fertilisation and development.

questions.question: Which of the following methods works by preventing the meeting of gametes?
questions.explanation: Barrier methods physically prevent sperm from reaching the ovum; they also protect against STIs — the only contraception with dual benefit.

questions.question: The 'family planning' programme in India was initiated in
questions.explanation: India was among the first countries to launch a national family planning programme, later broadened into Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) care.

questions.question: MTP is relatively safe during
questions.explanation: The risk rises with gestational age, so MTP is safest early; it is performed to remove a pregnancy that is unwanted or harmful to mother or foetus.

questions.question: ICSI involves
options: transfer of a zygote into the tube
direct injection of a single sperm into the ovum
transfer of gametes into the tube
questions.explanation: Intra-cytoplasmic sperm injection is used when the male has very low sperm count or poor sperm motility — one sperm is enough.

questions.question: The law of segregation states that
options: alleles of a pair separate during gamete formation, so each gamete gets only one
questions.explanation: Segregation explains the 3:1 monohybrid and 9:3:3:1 dihybrid ratios; it is a direct consequence of the separation of homologous chromosomes in anaphase I.

questions.question: A dihybrid cross in which both parents are heterozygous gives a phenotypic ratio of
questions.explanation: 9:3:3:1 comes from independent assortment of two genes. A test cross of a dihybrid, by contrast, gives 1:1:1:1.

questions.question: In snapdragon, a cross between red and white flowers gives pink flowers in F1. This is
questions.explanation: The heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype and the F2 ratio is 1:2:1 (red:pink:white) — no allele is completely dominant.

questions.question: AB blood group in humans is an example of
questions.explanation: Both A and B antigens are expressed because the alleles I^A and I^B are co-dominant, and I^O is recessive — three alleles, six genotypes, four phenotypes.

questions.question: Haemophilia in humans is
questions.explanation: Because it is X-linked recessive, males (having only one X) are affected far more often than females; a carrier mother transmits it to half her sons.

questions.question: Down syndrome is caused by
questions.explanation: Karyotype 47 with trisomy 21; features include a short stature, furrowed tongue and palm crease, with intellectual disability.

questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia results from
options: a single base substitution replacing glutamic acid with valine in the beta-globin chain
questions.explanation: Under low oxygen the abnormal haemoglobin polymerises and RBCs become sickle-shaped — a classic example of a point mutation causing disease.

questions.question: Polygenic inheritance is best illustrated by
questions.explanation: Several genes each add a small effect, giving continuous variation (a bell-shaped curve), unlike the discrete categories of single-gene traits.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Principles of Inheritance and Variation

questions.question: The number of gamete types produced by an individual of genotype AaBb (genes unlinked) is
questions.explanation: 2^n where n is the number of heterozygous genes: 2² = 4 (AB, Ab, aB, ab) — each in equal proportion.

questions.question: Colour blindness in humans is
options: X-linked recessive, more common in males
questions.explanation: A colour-blind man cannot pass the trait to his sons (he gives them Y) but passes the carrier state to all his daughters.

questions.question: Klinefelter's syndrome has the karyotype
questions.explanation: XXY males are sterile with gynaecomastia and some feminine features. Turner (45, XO) females are sterile with rudimentary ovaries.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Mendelian disorder?
questions.explanation: Mendelian disorders are due to single gene mutations (haemophilia, thalassaemia, sickle cell anaemia, PKU, colour blindness); the others are chromosomal.

questions.question: Linkage was discovered by
questions.explanation: Morgan showed that genes on the same chromosome are linked and do not assort independently — his recombination frequencies measured genetic distance.

questions.question: Sex determination in birds is
questions.explanation: In birds (and some reptiles), females are ZW and males ZZ — the reverse of humans, where males are XY. Grasshoppers use XO.

questions.question: The distance between two consecutive base pairs in B-DNA is
questions.explanation: Pitch = 3.4 nm with 10 bp per turn, so each base pair rises 0.34 nm; the diameter of the helix is 2 nm.

questions.question: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine using
questions.explanation: A=T has two H-bonds while G≡C has three — which is exactly why GC-rich DNA has a higher melting temperature.

questions.question: The transforming principle in Griffith's experiment was
questions.explanation: Avery, MacLeod and McCarty then showed biochemically that the transforming substance was DNA — purified and proved.

questions.question: Hershey and Chase used radioactive isotopes to show that
options: DNA is the genetic material using 32P and 35S
questions.explanation: 32P labelled DNA and 35S labelled protein of the bacteriophage; only the 32P entered the bacteria and appeared in the progeny.

questions.question: DNA replication is
questions.explanation: Proved by Meselson and Stahl in E. coli using 15N. Each new DNA has one old strand and one new strand — hence 'semi-conservative'.

questions.question: The enzyme that unwinds the DNA double helix during replication is
questions.explanation: Helicase unwinds, DNA polymerase synthesises (5'→3'), ligase joins the Okazaki fragments, and primase lays down the RNA primer.

questions.question: The start codon in mRNA is
questions.explanation: AUG codes for methionine and starts translation; UAA, UAG and UGA are the three stop codons — the code is unambiguous and non-overlapping.

questions.question: The lac operon is an example of
options: negative regulation by a repressor that is inactivated by the inducer
questions.explanation: In the absence of lactose the repressor binds the operator and blocks transcription; lactose (as allolactose) inactivates the repressor — a classic inducible system.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Molecular Basis of Inheritance

questions.question: The number of nucleotides in one turn of the B-DNA helix is
questions.explanation: 10 base pairs per turn with a pitch of 3.4 nm — two of the most-repeated numbers in this chapter.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of the genetic code?
questions.explanation: The code is triplet, degenerate (more than one codon per amino acid), non-overlapping, comma-less and nearly universal — but never overlapping.

questions.question: Eukaryotic mRNA undergoes
questions.explanation: Split genes have exons and introns: introns are removed by splicing, and a 5' cap and poly-A tail are added for stability.

questions.question: Which enzyme synthesises RNA in eukaryotes?
questions.explanation: RNA pol I makes rRNA, pol II makes mRNA (hnRNA) and pol III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNA.

questions.question: Satellite DNA is useful in DNA fingerprinting because it
options: shows a high degree of polymorphism in repeat number
questions.explanation: VNTR (variable number tandem repeats) differ between individuals, giving each person a unique band pattern — used in forensic identification.

questions.question: The Human Genome Project revealed that the human genome has about
questions.explanation: About 3164.7 million base pairs and ~30,000 genes; only 1.4% of DNA codes for proteins, the rest being repetitive or non-coding.

practiceSets.name: 🩺 NEET Drill — Evolution

questions.question: Homologous organs are those that have
options: the same fundamental structure but different functions
different structures but the same function
the same structure and the same function
questions.explanation: Homology indicates divergent evolution from a common ancestor: the forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans are the classic example.

questions.question: Analogous organs indicate
options: convergent evolution, as in the wings of a butterfly and a bird
questions.explanation: Similar function but different structure and ancestry — they show how different lineages solve the same problem independently.

questions.question: Which of the following is a vestigial organ in humans?
questions.explanation: Vestigial organs are reduced and functionless remnants, still present in the body — evidence of descent with modification.

questions.question: The Miller-Urey experiment demonstrated
options: the abiotic formation of amino acids from simple gases and energy sources
questions.explanation: Electric discharge in a mixture of CH4, H2, NH3 and water vapour produced amino acids — supporting the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis.

questions.question: Darwin's finches of the Galapagos Islands are an example of
questions.explanation: From a single ancestral seed-eating bird, different beak types evolved for different food sources — radiation to fill new niches.

questions.question: Industrial melanism in Biston betularia demonstrated
options: natural selection favouring dark moths in polluted (soot-covered) areas
questions.explanation: Post-industrialisation, soot covered the tree trunks, so dark moths were better camouflaged; the frequency of the dark form rose sharply.

questions.question: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is disturbed by
options: all of these: mutation, gene flow, genetic drift and natural selection
questions.explanation: The principle states that allele frequencies stay constant only in the absence of these evolutionary forces — the theory is a null model for change.

questions.question: The correct sequence of human evolution (from earliest) is
options: Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Australopithecus → Homo sapiens
Dryopithecus → Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens
questions.explanation: Cranial capacities rise along this line: Homo habilis ≈ 650–800 cc, Homo erectus ≈ 900 cc, Neanderthal ≈ 1400 cc, Homo sapiens ≈ 1300–1600 cc.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Evolution

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of homology?
options: Wings of a butterfly and wings of a bird
Thorns of Bougainvillea and tendrils of Cucurbita
The vertebral column of a fish and of a human
questions.explanation: Butterfly and bird wings perform the same function (flight) with different structures and independent origins — they are analogous. The other three pairs share the same fundamental plan (homologous).

questions.question: Genetic drift is
options: a random change in allele frequency in a small population
a change caused by mutation only
questions.explanation: The founder effect is a special case: a few individuals colonise a new area and their allele frequencies differ from the parent population.

questions.question: According to the big bang theory, the universe is about
questions.explanation: NCERT describes the universe as approximately 20 billion years old, with the earth formed about 4.5 billion years ago.

questions.question: The first cellular forms of life appeared on earth about
questions.explanation: NCERT states that the first cellular forms of life appeared about 2000 million years ago, with eukaryotes appearing later and invertebrates around 500 mya.

questions.question: Sickle cell anaemia persists at high frequency in malaria-endemic regions of Africa because
options: heterozygotes have resistance to malaria (balanced polymorphism)
the mutation is beneficial in homozygotes
questions.explanation: The heterozygote advantage keeps the allele in the population — an example of natural selection maintaining a harmful allele.

questions.question: Which of the following about Ramapithecus is correct?
options: It was more ape-like and existed 3 mya
It was more man-like and existed about 15 mya
questions.explanation: Dryopithecus was more ape-like; Ramapithecus (15 mya) was more man-like and walked on two legs, with a small cranium.

questions.question: Malaria is caused by
options: Plasmodium species transmitted by the female Anopheles mosquito
questions.explanation: P. vivax, P. falciparum and P. malariae are the malarial parasites. The toxic pigment haemozoin causes the chill and recurrent fever.

questions.question: The Widal test is used for the diagnosis of
questions.explanation: Salmonella typhi (the typhoid pathogen) is confirmed by the Widal test. Typhoid Mary, a carrier, spread the disease through food she cooked.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a viral disease?
questions.explanation: Pneumonia is caused by bacteria (Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae); the common cold is due to rhinoviruses.

questions.question: Filariasis (elephantiasis) is caused by
options: Wuchereria species, transmitted by female Culex mosquitoes
questions.explanation: The worms block lymphatic vessels, causing swelling of the legs and genital organs — a common disease in tropical regions.

questions.question: Innate immunity includes
options: physical barriers, phagocytic cells and inflammation
questions.explanation: Innate immunity is non-specific and present from birth; acquired immunity is pathogen-specific, has memory and involves B and T lymphocytes.

questions.question: Antibodies are produced by
questions.explanation: The antibody molecule (= H2L2) is a protein made of two heavy and two light chains. T cells help B cells and kill infected cells directly (cell-mediated immunity).

questions.question: The virus that causes AIDS destroys
questions.explanation: HIV is a retrovirus with reverse transcriptase; it infects and destroys helper T cells, leading to progressive immune deficiency and opportunistic infections.

questions.question: Interferons are
options: proteins secreted by virus-infected cells that protect neighbouring uninfected cells
questions.explanation: Interferons give non-specific viral resistance — the body's early antiviral alarm system before specific antibodies appear.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Human Health and Disease

questions.question: Which of the following is an autoimmune disease?
questions.explanation: In autoimmunity the immune system attacks self-molecules. Myasthenia gravis is the second NCERT example.

questions.question: Cancer cells differ from normal cells in
options: losing contact inhibition and dividing uncontrollably, with metastasis
questions.explanation: Loss of contact inhibition lets cells pile up into tumours; metastasis spreads them to distant sites — the most feared property of malignant tumours.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms causes ringworm?
questions.explanation: These fungi grow in moist, warm skin folds and are transmitted by touching contaminated objects; ringworm is not caused by a worm at all.

questions.question: Colostrum is important for the newborn because it contains
questions.explanation: The yellowish first milk supplies passive immunity (IgA) — preformed antibodies that protect until the infant's own immune system develops.

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary lymphoid organ?
questions.explanation: Primary lymphoid organs (bone marrow, thymus) are where lymphocytes mature; secondary organs (spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches) are where they meet antigens.

questions.question: Cocaine is obtained from
questions.explanation: Cocaine interferes with dopamine transport in the brain, producing euphoria; heroin comes from the opium poppy and cannabinoids from Cannabis.

questions.question: Curd is formed from milk by
options: Lactobacillus bacteria, which also improve its nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B12
questions.explanation: LAB curdle milk by producing lactic acid; they also check disease-causing microbes in the stomach — the reason curd is called a probiotic.

questions.question: The microbe used in baking and in the brewing industry is
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments dough sugars to CO2 (raising the dough) and produces ethanol in brewing — one organism, two industries.

questions.question: Penicillin was discovered by
questions.explanation: Fleming noticed the mould inhibiting bacterial growth in 1928; Chain and Florey turned it into a usable drug — the first antibiotic.

questions.question: Citric acid is produced industrially by
questions.explanation: Learn the acid-microbe pairs: Aspergillus niger → citric acid, Acetobacter aceti → acetic acid, Clostridium butylicum → butyric acid, Lactobacillus → lactic acid.

questions.question: The 'Swiss cheese' characteristic holes are formed by
options: Propionibacterium sharmanii, which produces large amounts of CO2
questions.explanation: Roquefort cheese uses Penicillium roqueforti; Swiss cheese uses Propionibacterium sharmanii — a classic two-way matching question.

questions.question: Cyclosporin A, an immunosuppressive agent used in organ transplants, is obtained from
questions.explanation: Statins, which lower blood cholesterol, come from Monascus purpureus. Both are bioactive molecules from fungi.

questions.question: BOD is a measure of
options: the number of bacteria in water
the amount of oxygen consumed by bacteria to oxidise the organic matter in water
questions.explanation: High BOD means more organic pollution. Treated sewage has a much lower BOD than untreated sewage.

questions.question: In the secondary treatment of sewage, the floating masses of bacteria are called
options: flocs, which are then used to form activated sludge
questions.explanation: Flocs of microbes digest organic matter in the aeration tank; part of the activated sludge is recycled as inoculum and the rest is digested anaerobically.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Microbes in Human Welfare

questions.question: Biogas is chiefly a mixture of
questions.explanation: Methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow anaerobically on cellulosic waste and produce CH4-rich gas — used as fuel in rural areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is used as a biocontrol agent against aphids?
questions.explanation: Ladybirds and dragonflies prey on aphids and mosquitoes; Bacillus thuringiensis controls caterpillars, Trichoderma works against root pathogens and NPV against insects.

questions.question: Rhizobium is a biofertiliser that
options: fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes
questions.explanation: Rhizobium lives symbiotically in the root nodules of leguminous plants; Azotobacter is free-living and fixes nitrogen in the soil.

questions.question: Mycorrhiza is a symbiotic association between
options: fungi and plant roots that improves phosphorus absorption
questions.explanation: Glomus species form mycorrhizae; they help in phosphorus uptake, drought tolerance and mineral absorption — a natural biofertiliser.

questions.question: The activated sludge process is
options: an aerobic secondary treatment step in sewage treatment
a tertiary step to remove nutrients
questions.explanation: Air is pumped into the aeration tank, bacteria grow as flocs and oxidise organic matter; the sludge is then digested anaerobically to produce biogas.

questions.question: Bacillus thuringiensis is used to control
questions.explanation: The bacterium's toxin (from a cry gene) kills the larvae of insects such as the tobacco budworm and corn borer — the basis of Bt cotton.

questions.question: Restriction endonucleases are used in genetic engineering because they
options: cut DNA at specific palindromic recognition sequences
questions.explanation: They are called 'molecular scissors'. Ligase is the enzyme that joins fragments — do not mix the two up.

questions.question: EcoRI cuts DNA to produce
options: sticky ends that can be joined by ligase
questions.explanation: The staggered cut leaves short single-stranded overhangs (sticky ends) that base-pair with complementary ends of the vector — the basis of cloning.

questions.question: In the name EcoRI, the letter 'R' stands for
options: the strain of the bacterium (RY13) from which it was isolated
questions.explanation: Eco = Escherichia coli, R = strain, I = the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain — the full standard nomenclature.

questions.question: A good cloning vector must have
options: an origin of replication, a selectable marker, restriction sites and a small size
questions.explanation: Ori gives autonomous replication, the selectable marker helps identify transformants, and unique restriction sites are where the insert goes.

questions.question: Insertional inactivation in pBR322 is detected by
options: loss of tetracycline resistance when the insert disrupts that gene
questions.explanation: pBR322 has ampicillin and tetracycline resistance genes: a recombinant plasmid loses one resistance, and recombinants are recombinants because they are ampicillin-resistant but tetracycline-sensitive.

questions.question: PCR involves the three steps
options: denaturation, annealing and extension repeated in cycles
questions.explanation: Temperatures: about 94 °C to separate the strands, 50–55 °C for primers to anneal, 72 °C for Taq polymerase to extend — a billion-fold amplification in about 30 cycles.

questions.question: Stirred-tank bioreactors are preferred because they
options: allow better mixing of oxygen and uniform growth of cells
questions.explanation: A mechanically stirred tank ensures even aeration and mixing; the sparged bioreactor mixes by bubbling air instead.

questions.question: Making bacterial cells competent for transformation involves
options: treatment with divalent cations such as Ca²⁺ followed by a brief heat shock
questions.explanation: Other methods include micro-injection, biolistics (gene guns) and using disarmed plant pathogen vectors such as Agrobacterium tumefaciens.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a tool of recombinant DNA technology?
questions.explanation: The tools are restriction enzymes, polymerases, ligases, vectors and competent hosts. Chitinase digests chitin (a fungal wall enzyme), not DNA.

questions.question: Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments according to
options: size, with smaller fragments moving farther
questions.explanation: Negatively charged DNA moves towards the anode through the agarose gel; staining with ethidium bromide and UV light makes the bands visible.

questions.question: The first transgenic cow produced human protein-enriched milk. The protein was
questions.explanation: Rosie, the first transgenic cow (1997), produced milk containing human alpha-lactalbumin — a landmark in molecular farming.

questions.question: Which enzyme joins the DNA fragments during cloning?
questions.explanation: Ligase seals the phosphodiester backbone between the insert and the vector. Unlike restriction enzymes, it needs ATP.

questions.question: Downstream processing includes
options: separation, purification and formulation of the product with quality control
questions.explanation: After the bioreactor, the product must be separated from biomass, purified and formulated — this stage is why biotech drugs are expensive.

questions.question: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is used in plant biotechnology because
options: it naturally transfers its Ti plasmid DNA into plant cells
questions.explanation: Its Ti plasmid is a natural gene-delivery vehicle; scientists disarm the tumour-inducing genes and insert the desired gene instead.

questions.question: Bt cotton is resistant to bollworm because
options: the cry genes of Bacillus thuringiensis make the plant produce a toxin that solubilises in the alkaline insect gut
the plant absorbs insecticide from the soil
questions.explanation: The inactive protoxin is converted into active toxin only in the alkaline, warm gut of the insect — the bacterium itself is protected because it lacks that environment.

questions.question: Human insulin (Humulin) is produced by
options: inserting the A and B chain genes of insulin into E. coli
questions.explanation: Eli Lilly (1983) produced two DNA sequences for chains A and B, expressed them in E. coli and joined the chains by disulphide bonds — the first genetically engineered medicine.

questions.question: Gene therapy for ADA deficiency involves
options: introducing the functional ADA gene into lymphocytes removed from the patient and returning them
questions.explanation: ADA deficiency is a rare inherited immune disorder. Permanent cure requires gene transfer into bone marrow cells at an early age — the first clinical gene therapy (1990).

questions.question: RNA interference (RNAi) is used to
options: silence a specific gene by introducing complementary dsRNA
questions.explanation: In tobacco plants, RNAi against the nematode Meloidogyne incognita prevents the parasite from surviving — a parasite-specific resistance strategy.

questions.question: ELISA is based on
questions.explanation: ELISA detects antigens or antibodies using an enzyme-linked colour reaction; PCR detects very low amounts of pathogen DNA by amplification.

questions.question: Flavr Savr tomato was developed for
options: delayed ripening and a longer shelf life
questions.explanation: Flavr Savr (1994) was the first commercially grown GM food; antisense RNA technology slowed down the ripening process.

questions.question: The 'cry' genes of Bacillus thuringiensis code for
options: insecticidal proteins produced as inactive protoxins
questions.explanation: Different cry genes (cryIAc, cryIIAb) target different insects; the protoxin becomes an active toxin only in the alkaline gut of the insect.

questions.question: GEAC in India is responsible for
options: approving the release of genetically modified organisms into the environment
questions.explanation: The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (now GEAC) is a statutory body that evaluates GM research and its safety before release.

questions.question: Biopiracy refers to
options: the use of bio-resources by organisations without authorisation or compensation to the country of origin
questions.explanation: Biopiracy is exploitation plus patenting — India's patent offence cases include Basmati rice, turmeric and neem.

questions.question: Golden rice is a genetically modified variety developed for
questions.explanation: Golden rice aims at dietary vitamin A deficiency in developing countries; Bt crops, by contrast, carry pest resistance genes.

questions.question: Transgenic animals are used to
options: study diseases, produce biological products and test vaccine safety and chemical toxicity
questions.explanation: Transgenic animals carry a foreign gene; they are research models rather than products — the classic NCERT uses are the four listed here.

questions.question: The first transgenic cow Rosie was used to produce
questions.explanation: Rosie's milk contained 2.4 g of human alpha-lactalbumin per litre — a proof that animals can be living bioreactors.

questions.question: Molecular diagnosis by PCR is preferred over conventional methods because
options: it can detect very low concentrations of pathogen DNA at an early stage
questions.explanation: PCR amplifies trace amounts of DNA, so infections can be detected before symptoms appear — extremely important for diseases like HIV and tuberculosis.

questions.question: Which technique uses radioactive DNA probes for detection?
questions.explanation: A labelled DNA probe hybridises with the pathogen DNA and its position is visualised by autoradiography — used in detecting mutant genes and in DNA fingerprinting.

questions.question: Commensalism is an interaction in which
options: one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited
one is harmed and the other unaffected
questions.explanation: Signs: +/0. The orchid growing on a mango branch and barnacles on a whale are the NCERT examples.

questions.question: In amensalism
options: one species is harmed and the other is unaffected
one benefits and one is harmed
questions.explanation: Signs: −/0, as when a large tree shades out a smaller plant. By contrast, predation and parasitism are +/−.

questions.question: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that
options: two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot coexist indefinitely
questions.explanation: The superior competitor eliminates the inferior one. Resource partitioning (as in MacArthur's warblers) is one way coexistence is achieved.

questions.question: The exponential growth equation is
questions.explanation: r = intrinsic rate of natural increase; exponential growth gives a J-shaped curve and assumes unlimited resources.

questions.question: In the logistic growth model, K represents
options: the carrying capacity of the environment
the population size at time zero
questions.explanation: Logistic growth produces an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve that levels off at K. Resources are finite in nature, so real populations follow this model better.

questions.question: Ectotherms are animals that
options: maintain a constant body temperature internally
regulate their body temperature by behaviour, using environmental heat
questions.explanation: Ectotherms (reptiles, fishes, amphibians) vs endotherms (birds, mammals) — a favourite one-line distinction in the ecology chapter.

questions.question: Predation between two species always results in
options: a +/− interaction where the predator benefits and prey is harmed
questions.explanation: Predators keep prey populations in check (biological control) and are the first examples of energy transfer between trophic levels.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of mutualism?
options: A large tree shading a smaller plant
questions.explanation: Both partners benefit (+/+): the alga photosynthesises and the fungus provides shelter and minerals. Cuscuta is a parasite; the orchid is commensal.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Organisms and Populations

questions.question: The relationship between a fig tree and its wasp pollinator is an example of
options: mutualism, where the wasp pollinates and uses the fruit for laying eggs
questions.explanation: Each fig species has its own wasp species — the classic obligate mutualism described in NCERT's 'expanding horizons' box.

questions.question: Parasitism differs from predation in that
options: the parasite is smaller and, in most cases, does not kill the host immediately
parasites live outside the body only
questions.explanation: Parasites are host-specific and derive nutrition from the host; ectoparasites (lice) live outside and endoparasites (tapeworm) live inside.

questions.question: Age pyramids with a broad base indicate
options: a growing population, with more young individuals than older ones
questions.explanation: A broad base means high natality. A bell-shaped pyramid means a stable population, and an urn shape means declining numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a conformer strategy?
options: Birds that maintain constant body temperature
Small animals whose body temperature changes with the environment
questions.explanation: Conformers cannot regulate their internal environment; regulators use thermoregulation and osmoregulation to maintain a constant internal state.

questions.question: Resource partitioning allows coexistence because
options: the two species use different parts of the resource at different times
questions.explanation: MacArthur's five warblers of the same tree divided themselves among different zones — competition was avoided by using different microhabitats.

questions.question: Which of the following is a population attribute?
options: Natality, mortality, sex ratio and age distribution
questions.explanation: Population attributes are properties of the group as a whole, and ecological density depends on both numbers and the area they occupy.

questions.question: Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses equals
questions.explanation: NPP is the biomass available to herbivores and decomposers. GPP = NPP + respiration (R).

questions.question: According to the 10% law of energy transfer, the energy available to the next trophic level is about
options: 10% of that at the previous level
questions.explanation: Lindeman's 10% law explains why food chains are short: with 10,000 J at the producer level, a top carnivore gets only 10 J after three transfers.

questions.question: The five steps of decomposition in the correct order are
questions.explanation: Warm and moist conditions with nitrogen-rich, low-lignin litter give the fastest decomposition rates.

questions.question: Which of the following ecological pyramids is always upright?
questions.explanation: Energy decreases at each trophic level following the second law of thermodynamics, so its pyramid can never be inverted — a favourite NCERT line.

questions.question: In an ecosystem, the process of mineralisation
options: releases inorganic nutrients from the humus into the soil
questions.explanation: Humification creates dark, resistant humus; mineralisation then liberates the inorganic nutrients for reuse by plants.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sedimentary nutrient cycle?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus has no gaseous phase — it circulates through rock, soil, water and organisms; carbon and nitrogen are gaseous cycles with atmospheric reservoirs.

questions.question: Pioneer species in primary succession on bare rock (xerarch) are usually
options: lichens that secrete acids and weather the rock
questions.explanation: Lichens are followed by bryophytes, then herbs, shrubs and finally trees. In hydrarch succession, the pioneers are phytoplankton.

questions.question: Ecosystem services include
options: purification of air and water, pollination and carbon fixation — worth trillions of dollars
questions.explanation: Robert Constanza's 1997 estimate put the value of ecosystem services at about 33 trillion US dollars a year — a key NCERT 'expanding horizons' figure.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Ecosystem

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a decomposer?
questions.explanation: Decomposers are saprophytic organisms (fungi and bacteria are the main ones; earthworms help fragmentation). A cow is a primary consumer.

questions.question: The grazing food chain (GFC) and detritus food chain (DFC) are connected because
options: dead organisms from GFC become detritus for DFC, and vice versa
DFC has no relation to GFC
questions.explanation: Together they form the energy-flow network of the ecosystem — in some ecosystems, the DFC receives more energy than the GFC.

questions.question: The biological magnification of toxic substances is highest at
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable pollutants accumulate at each step because they are not excreted — hence the high concentrations in birds of prey and humans.

questions.question: In a grassland ecosystem the pyramid of numbers is
options: always inverted at the second level
questions.explanation: Grass (many) → insects/herbivores → carnivores is upright. A tree ecosystem gives an inverted pyramid of numbers (one tree supports many insects).

questions.question: Detritus food chain begins with
questions.explanation: DFC: detritus → decomposers. It is the dominant pathway in some terrestrial and most aquatic ecosystems.

questions.question: Nutrient cycling is faster in

practiceSets.name: 🩺 NEET Drill — Biodiversity and Conservation

questions.question: The three levels of biodiversity are
questions.explanation: Genetic diversity is variation within a species (rice varieties); species diversity is variation between species; ecosystem diversity is variation in habitats.

questions.question: According to the species-area relationship, the equation is
options: log S = log C + Z log A
log A = log S + Z log C
questions.explanation: S = richness, A = area, Z = slope (regression coefficient). Steep Z values (0.6–1.2) are typical for very large areas such as continents.

questions.question: The latitudinal gradient of biodiversity means that
options: it decreases from the poles to the equator
species diversity decreases from the equator toward the poles
questions.explanation: Tropical regions have more species because of a longer evolutionary time, more solar energy and greater productivity; the Amazon is the richest.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most important cause of biodiversity loss?
questions.explanation: The 'Evil Quartet': habitat loss and fragmentation tops the list, followed by over-exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinctions.

questions.question: The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria caused
options: extinction of many native cichlid fish species
a decrease in water quality only
questions.explanation: An alien species introduction that wiped out the endemic cichlids — one of NCERT's most-quoted examples of species invasion.

questions.question: Which of the following is an in-situ conservation method?
options: Biosphere reserves, national parks and sacred groves
questions.explanation: In-situ = conserving species in their natural habitat; ex-situ = conserving them outside (zoo, botanical garden, gene bank, cryopreservation).

questions.question: The rivet popper hypothesis about biodiversity was proposed by
questions.explanation: Ehrlich compared an ecosystem to an aeroplane held together by rivets: losing a few rivets (species) may be survivable, but losing key ones (canopy species) crashes the plane.

questions.question: The number of biodiversity hotspots in India is
questions.explanation: There are 34 global hotspots (Myers), of which three lie in India. Two more regions — Sundaland and Wallacea — are sometimes listed for their Indian portions.

practiceSets.name: 🎯 PYQ Drill — Biodiversity and Conservation

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an ex-situ conservation method?
questions.explanation: A national park is in-situ (the species stays in its habitat). Zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks and cryopreservation are all ex-situ.

questions.question: In the species-area relationship, the slope Z for a small area such as within a continent typically falls between
questions.explanation: Within a continent or a small region, Z = 0.1–0.2; for very large areas spanning whole continents, Z = 0.6–1.2 — a frequently asked pair.

questions.question: Co-extinction refers to
options: extinction of a species due to the extinction of another species it depends on
mass extinction at the end of an era
questions.explanation: When a host or mutualist disappears, its dependent partner follows — as with a fig and its specific wasp pollinator.

questions.question: The IUCN Red List documents
options: species facing the risk of extinction with their conservation status
questions.explanation: Categories range from 'Least Concern' to 'Critically Endangered', 'Extinct in the Wild' and 'Extinct' — a worldwide conservation index.

questions.question: Sacred groves are
options: forest patches protected by local communities on religious grounds
questions.explanation: They are an in-situ tradition of conservation (for example, in the Western Ghats and Meghalaya) and preserve rich biodiversity along with culture.

questions.question: Which international convention deals with the conservation of biodiversity?
questions.explanation: The CBD was signed at the Rio Earth Summit, where nations agreed to sustainable use and equitable sharing of biodiversity benefits.
